text:
ana-cs: FYI we just got a support escalation from VelvetShop — their order confirmation emails are showing prices like "$0.00" or missing decimals after last week's model rollout. Customer says it started ~2026-02-10.

tom-support: ACK. Can you paste their exact examples? ask them for the original user input + the model output + the request_id if available. also ask what model they were pinned to (hosted or dedicated).

ana-cs: customer sent 3 examples in the ticket. I'm pasting redacted snippets below (they asked us not to include customer emails in slack):

Customer-provided sample 1 (redacted):
```
User: "Please show order total for order #98765"
Model: "Order total: $0.00"
Request id: 63f4b7a2
```

Customer-provided sample 2 (redacted):
```
User: "Cart total for 3 items"
Model: "Total: $0"
Request id: 63f4b9d8
```

ana-cs: They say they were on the hosted API and did not pin a revision — just using the default `gpt-open-2048` alias.

deepak-ml: Thanks. Two quick asks to triage: 1) full request logs (request body + response tokens) for one of the request ids, 2) model_revision returned in the response headers for those calls.

ana-cs: I asked customer to send the full request log for request id 63f4b7a2 and to confirm header `x-rd-model-revision`. I also asked them to run a minimal repro below and paste the request id back. waiting on reply.

lia-prod: ops-bot did a canary deploy last Thursday night (2026-02-06 03:40 UTC) for `gpt-open-2048` with quantization kernel tweak. Canary at 10% for 6h, then 100% rollout by 2026-02-06 11:30 UTC. No rollback recorded.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed gpt-open-2048@rev-20260206-quant-opt to production. Canary window: 10% (2026-02-06T03:40Z -> 2026-02-06T09:40Z). Full rollout: 2026-02-06T11:32Z.

deepak-ml: That timing matches the customer report. Suspect a change in numeric formatting behavior after kernel/quantization adjustment. Could be tokenization edge-case that causes trailing decimals to drop for certain prompt patterns.

ana-cs: Customer replied with the full log for 63f4b7a2 but redacted PII. They included the request body and response (tokens list). Pasting redacted log excerpt here:
```
{"prompt":"Summarize order: items -> [redacted] \nCalculate total:","max_tokens":64,"temperature":0.0}
Response tokens: ["Order"," total",":"," \"$","0",".","00\""]
Model header x-rd-model-revision: rev-20260206-quant-opt
```

tom-support: The tokens show `"$","0",".","00"` — the model produced the right tokenization, but customer sees only `$0.00` or `$0` sometimes. Are there post-processing hooks in their app that could be trimming/formatting currency? Also check if streaming or chunked responses might reassemble incorrectly.

deepak-ml: Good point. Two parallel investigations:
- I'll run the same prompt against a pinned pre-rollout revision (`rev-20260120-stable`) and the post-rollout (`rev-20260206-quant-opt`) with identical seeds/args to compare token-level outputs.
- Can we get their raw bytes for the API response (not just the joined string)? streaming boundaries might drop punctuation in some SDKs.

lia-prod: infra: can we surface the raw response payload for the request id 63f4b7a2 from our logs? retention is enabled for CS escalations.

ops-bot: log-bot: Retrieved log artifact for request id 63f4b7a2. s3://rd-logs/prod/requests/63f4b7a2/raw.json (redacted link shared privately to CS).

ana-cs: Customer ran the minimal repro we asked and pasted the new request id: 63f504001. They used the same prompt with `temperature:0`. They also confirmed they were NOT doing any client-side currency formatting.

deepak-ml: I ran the two revisions locally. Quick summary:
- rev-20260120-stable => tokens: ["Order"," total",":"," \"$","12",".","34\""] => joined => "Order total: \"$12.34\""
- rev-20260206-quant-opt => tokens: ["Order"," total",":"," \"$","12",".","34\""] => joined => "Order total: \"$12.34\""
So core model output looks identical for that prompt. That suggests the model is producing decimals correctly in many cases.

tom-support: but customer still has examples with missing decimals. Could be input-sensitive. Ask CS to collect the original user inputs that preceded the failure cases (we only had the short prompts). Also request `content-length` and whether they used streaming; streaming could cause client concat bugs.

ana-cs: will do. I also asked them to run a deterministic test with `stream=false` and `logprobs=1` and send the request id. Provided this curl snippet to the customer:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-2048","prompt":"Summarize order: items -> [REDACTED]\nCalculate total:","temperature":0.0,"stream":false,"logprobs":1}'
```

ops-bot: reminder: if customer shares logs with PII, instruct them to redact with `[REDACTED]` and include at least one reproducible minimal-case that is safe to share.

deepak-ml: One more internal check: I'll search for other tickets referencing `rev-20260206-quant-opt` + currency in the last 2 weeks. If we see a cluster, we can escalate to infra to rollback the kernel tweak.

lia-prod: I'll also validate the canary telemetry for token boundary errors and check if any autoscaling events coincided with dropped streaming packets.

ana-cs: customer acknowledged and will run the curl with stream=false and send back the new request id. Marking thread "waiting on customer". I'll update here when they reply.

[thread status: waiting_on_customer]
